subject: Clarifying mid-cycle token attribution after EFT payment hold
messages:
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@privatenet.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: FinanceOps <finance@privatenet.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 09:23:00 -0500
Subject: Unexpected mid-cycle usage spike + EFT hold question

Hi Jordan,

We noticed a sharp jump in token consumption in the first week of November and an adjacent mid-cycle adjustment on the Dec 1 invoice. Our finance team also shows an EFT payment submitted on Nov 30 that was temporarily held for verification (see attached payment_notifications.pdf). Two questions:

1) Can you share the raw per-session/token logs for Nov 28–Dec 2 so we can match against our ingestion?
2) Is there any known behavior where an EFT hold could trigger delayed attribution or cause tokens to be billed to a fallback org/tenant?

We have a small engineering team available this afternoon to walk through anything you can pull. We flagged specific session IDs in our system (session-11738, session-11770) that seem duplicated on our side.

Thanks,

Liam O'Neill
Head of Platform Operations
Privatenet

Attachment: payment_notifications.pdf (PDF)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@privatenet.ai>
Cc: FinanceOps <finance@privatenet.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 10:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-cycle usage spike + EFT hold question

Hi Liam — thanks for the heads up and the attachment. We've received similar flags on our side and want to get you answers quickly.

Action plan:
- Ben (AE) will coordinate a short troubleshooting call with your engineering/finance team today.
- Priyom (billing ops) will pull token-level deltas and the per-shard ingestion map for Nov 28–Dec 2 and share a CSV export.
- I'll propose a temporary, one-time pro-rated credit if we confirm a misattribution while we correct the attribution logic.

Can you confirm whether the held EFT was ultimately cleared or remains in "verification" status with your bank? That will affect whether credits are applied as an offset or as a bill adjustment.

Best,

Jordan Blake
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2027 13:44:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-cycle usage spike + EFT hold question — preliminary findings

Team — preliminary triage notes below (pulling from ingestion logs and billing pipeline):

Summary of findings:
- We pulled the token deltas for Nov 28–Dec 2 and generated an export (usage_export_20271201-1207.csv).
- There is a batching anomaly in the VPC egress window between 2027-11-29T23:40:00Z and 2027-11-30T01:10:00Z where events from Privatenet's private cluster were re-ingested by two ingestion shards (shard-7 and shard-11). That resulted in ~3.9M duplicate tokens being attributed twice across two short-lived sessions.
- The duplication aligns with the payment hold timeframe because our processing pipeline triggered a reattach/replay attempt when it observed an unacknowledged delivery during the banking reconciliation window. The replay logic should not change org attribution, but a corner-case bug in our tenant-tag propagation allowed a few sessions to be associated with the fallback tenant id (org-temp-000).

Evidence (high level):
- Repeated session IDs: 11734–11790 present in both shards, with overlapping timestamps and identical token counts.
- Audit trace shows two delivery attempts for the same message batch at 2027-11-30T00:02:17Z and 2027-11-30T00:07:03Z.

Immediate remediation we recommend:
- Backfill the correct attribution by re-mapping org-temp-000 tokens to Privatenet for the affected session range. This will remove the duplicate billing delta.
- Patch the tenant-tag propagation in the replay codepath (short patch ready for testing).

Suggested customer-facing resolution:
- Apply a pro-rated credit for the duplicated tokens while we run the backfill (estimated credit: $6,200).
- If Privatenet's EFT remains held and they want the invoice adjusted immediately, we can apply the credit against the outstanding balance and issue a corrected invoice; otherwise credit will be applied on the next cycle after the EFT clears.

I've attached the CSV export for token-level inspection. Next steps: Jordan/Ben — coordinate with Liam on a short call to confirm the session IDs and authorize the backfill. Marissa — can you review the proposed $6,200 credit and sign off if it fits our credit policy?

Attachment: usage_export_20271201-1207.csv (CSV, 2.1MB)

Thanks,
Priyom
Billing Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@privatenet.ai>
Cc: FinanceOps <finance@privatenet.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2027 16:08:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-cycle usage spike + EFT hold question — next steps and credit

Hi Liam — quick update after our internal review. Thank you for flagging the specific session IDs; they helped us confirm the scope.

What happened (short):
- A replay triggered by an unacknowledged delivery during your EFT verification window caused duplicate ingestion across two shards. A bug in tenant-tag propagation allowed a small set of sessions to be billed to a fallback tenant, which resulted in duplicate token billing.

What we'll do now:
- We'll run a targeted backfill to reassign the ~3.9M duplicated tokens from org-temp-000 back to Privatenet and remove the duplicate line items from the Dec 1 invoice.
- We propose a one-time pro-rated credit of $6,200 while the backfill completes. If your EFT remains held and you prefer the invoice corrected immediately, we'll apply the credit against the outstanding balance and send a corrected invoice.
- Technical mitigation: the replay path patch from Priyom is queued for deploy to the staging cluster tomorrow; we'll follow up with an ETA for production deploy after internal testing.

Suggested next steps:
- Can we schedule a 20–30 minute sync Monday to walk through the CSV export and confirm the session mapping? Ben will coordinate times.
- Please confirm whether the EFT completed or is still in "verification" so we can finalize whether to offset the current outstanding balance or credit the next invoice.

Thanks again for your patience — we want to make this right quickly.

Regards,

Jordan Blake
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: usage_export_20271201-1207.csv (CSV), payment_notifications.pdf (PDF)
